        determine the completeness of the submitted documents and address any
        significant issues that may affect the construction cost or schedule.

Twenty five sheets of plans were provided to us and are considered a ‘builder set’,
        i.e., they are quite basic, as essentially the project is an ‘owner-builder’ as-well-as,
        ‘design-build’. Mechanical, electrical, plumbing and civil plans were missing from
        the drawing set provided to us.

The construction contract(s) provided is also a very basic document, lacking most
        clauses found in a typical AIA contract format. Two versions of the contract were
        provided. The contract is ‘cost plus’.

We were informed that work is well underway with framing near completion and
        interior drywall hung on one side of the walls, insulation is being installed, and
        rough mechanical, electrical and plumbing work is well underway. Roofing work is
        complete and elevator work is starting very soon. The GC expects the work to
        complete sooner than the published scheduled completion date of 2/28/13.

2.0     COST ANALYSIS

Based on the documents submitted, we have audited and reviewed the Direct
        Cost estimate for the construction of the subject project. In addition, we have
        prepared a conceptual cost estimate of the project based on the available plans
        and information.

Our estimate of the direct construction cost of the project (Hard cost, FF&E, A/E,
        Permits & Fees and Contingency) is $3,056,835 and is $638,906 or 26.42% higher
        than the comparable budget provided by the Borrower/Bank. This budget is
        attached as Appendix 3. The main reasons for this difference are as follows:

235b78bf0bfc.text:
   Contractor is self performing much of the work. This probably results in
                reduction in cost by 10% to 15%.
               Project is effectively an owner builder situation, even though the contracting
                entity and the Borrowing entity are different. The GC exclusively works for
                the Borrower.
               The budget for contingency is low.
               Budget for A/E is low.

PACS’s cost estimate summary is attached as Appendix 2.

Hard Cost of Construction

A one page estimate dated 9/10/12 indicates a hard cost of $2,370,519, which
        includes a contingency of $78,500. In addition, furnishings worth $100,000 and gym
        equipment worth $25,000 are also included. No GC fee and GC’s overhead are
        noted. However, some of the typical general conditions are noted separately in the
        budget.

We were informed that the GC will self perform much of the work, except the
        HVAC, fire sprinklers, paving, roofing, etc.

Our estimate of the ‘net’ (trade work) hard cost is 13.45% or $277,958 higher than
        the GC’s budget of $2,066,616.

Our estimate for the GC’s overhead and fee is 148% or $221,279 higher than the
        GC’s corresponding budget of $149,500. The GC’s budget is too low compared to
        market averages.

No third party GC will be able to complete the work for the contract amount of
        $2,370,519.

Owner’s Cost

FF&E

The GC’s contract includes a sum of $143,750 for the gym equipment and furniture
        and fixtures for the building. No detailed listing, purchase orders or contracts for
        FF&E were available to support the budget.

Government Fees & Permits

A sum of $20,153 is included in the GC’s budget for the mechanical and electrical
        permits only. No line item for actual building permits, miscellaneous permits and
        utility fees is noted. We have allowed a budget of $40,340.

Architecture & Engineering

The project is essentially design-build. The drawings are prepared by the contractor
        and are minimal in scope. A budget of $50,000 is included. We would expect
        market rate cost to be three times higher. We have reduced our estimate of the A/E
        fees by $60K to account for the ‘design-build’ approach and the level of details of
        the plans.

3.0     PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project involves the renovation of an existing two story facility with an
        area of 26,893 SF, into a Hollywood Production Center, located on a one flat lot. A
        site plan is attached as Appendix 6. The subject site consists of three legal land
        parcels and is 0.80 acres or 35,106 square feet in size. The site is rectangular in
        shape and is generally level and at street grade. The property is bordered by
        streets on three sides. Access to the site is provided via two driveways located
        on Lillian Way. The site will be fenced.

The building will be occupied by Hollywood Production Center, LLC (HPC), which is
        an Amidi related entity. Hollywood Production Center, LLC is a related party to the
        owner of the building. Hollywood Production Center, LLC is a business that
        provides immediate occupancy of creative office space and full service amenities
        for TV/film production, post-production, new media, and publishing companies.

5cfb9005f135.text:
The existing building was built in stages from 1935 thru 1970’s and is a class C
        improvement.      A complete renovation is proposed, which is underway.
        Approximately 44 feet by 46 feet new foundation with grade beams will be cast.
        Structural steel brace frames will be added above this foundation to seismically
        strengthen the existing structure. The building is a mix of reinforced poured in place
        concrete, wood frame, stucco exterior and concrete block. The building has
        conventional shallow spared footings and has fire sprinklers. Parking for the
        subject is provided in 58 surface parking spaces located at the rear of the site.
        The parking ratio is approximately 2.16 spaces per 1,000 rentable SF.

The first floor of the building has an area of 14,036 SF. It includes numerous rooms
        accessed via a corridor. The second floor has an area of 13,929 SF. This floor also
        will have numerous rooms. Access is provided via two sets of stairs. An elevator
        will be added to the building. The building has two sets of existing stairs. About
        1,960 SF of new area will be provided on the second floor. A set of restrooms will
        be provided on each floor. The second floor also has an employee exercise room
        with lockers and showers.

Additional project data is attached as Appendix 8.
